answer: A serial, non-parallelizable work chain resists Sybils: each newcomer completes small, verifiable jobs in strict order, each released only after the previous one is independently checked, like tracing a crystal vein that cannot be mined in parallel. Progress sits in a public reef of interlocking receipts, each referencing the last, so a farmer cannot reuse one job across identities. A plume of fresh, randomly chosen tasks arrives each epoch, and every step has a minimum real dwell time, so a hundred fake identities cost a hundred serial timelines, not one bulk run.
